neet_che_u08_t04_1.working: Units of k are (mol L^-1)^(1-n) s^-1. For n = 2 this gives L mol^-1 s^-1.

neet_che_u08_t04_2.working: Doubling [A] multiplies the rate by 4, so the order in A is 2. Tripling [B] multiplies the rate by 3, so the order in B is 1. Rate = k[A]^2[B].

neet_che_u08_t04_4.working: A is true: for first order, k = rate/[A], so the concentration units cancel and leave time^-1. R is true by definition (k equals the rate at unit concentrations). R does not explain why the unit is independent of the concentration unit, so it is not the correct explanation of A.

neet_che_u08_t04_5.working: I: (mol L^-1)^(1-n) = (mol L^-1)^(-1/2) gives n = 3/2, so I is correct. II: k in mol L^-1 s^-1 means zero order, so the rate is independent of concentration and II is correct.
